_comment: === TEST FILE: All four maintenance check types (A, B, C, D) forced within horizon ===
Design rationale:
AC0 — A check forced:  A_init=27001 min  (1 min overdue, threshold=27000 min)
AC1 — B check forced:  B_init=42001 min  (1 min overdue, threshold=42000 min)
AC2 — C check forced:  C_Days_init=600   (at threshold=600 calendar days)
AC3 — D check forced:  D_Days_init=2920  (at threshold=2920 calendar days)
AC4, AC5 — free aircraft (all zeros)
Horizon: 20 days (~28,800 min).  Only airport C has maintenance capacity.
KEY DESIGN: AC0-AC3 start at B so they can fly B->C directly as their check trigger.
C15(b) blocks aircraft AT C from departing C during their check window.
By starting at B, AC0-AC3 bypass C15(b) entirely — they fly B->C directly.
AC4, AC5 start at C to cover C->B outbound legs.
No forced checks on AC4/AC5 so C15(b) for day-1 never activates for them.
Flights f1-f4: B->C day-1 trigger flights (one per check-needing aircraft).
Flights f5-f8: C->B day-1 operational flights for AC4/AC5.
Flights f9-f12: later operational round-trips for AC0/AC4/AC5 post-check.
IMPORTANT: Run with --no-check-hierarchy so each aircraft gets its
designated check type, not a higher substitute.
Example command:
py -3 heu180h.py --data inpytABCD/ABCD_all_checks_test.json --no-check-hierarchy
Expected output (all four check types in events file):
AC0 -> A-check on day 1 (360 min, done by t=620)
AC1 -> B-check on day 1 (2880 min, continues into day 2-3)
AC2 -> C-check starting day 1 (20160 min = 14 days)
AC3 -> D-check starting day 1 (60480 min = 42 days, beyond 20-day horizon)
